assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore's collateral-constraint model shows how small shocks are amplified and persist through credit and asset-price feedback. It became a foundation of modern macro-finance, and it underlies much of the financial-friction work in policy models and in the literature on crises and the financial accelerator. I rate its depth and breadth of influence as very high.
assessment.attribution: The core idea belongs clearly to Kiyotaki and Moore (JPE 1997). Gertler and Gilchrist are important contributors to the financial accelerator and its empirical side, but that is a partly separate strand. Bernanke has already been recognised in 2022 for banking and crises. I therefore propose the cleanest two-person core.
assessment.maturity: About three decades of confirmation. The framework is standard in graduate macro and is validated by the 2008 crisis and its aftermath. No timing concern.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Gertler and Gilchrist for the empirical financial-accelerator strand.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises could weigh against it.
Gertler also appears under B029, so credit could be split across entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock studies and the task-based account of technology and labour demand changed how economists think about the distributional and local labour-market effects of trade and automation. They combine credible empirical design with a clear conceptual framework and have had large policy and public impact.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work is clearly Autor-Dorn-Hanson. The task-based framework is broader and also involves Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane, who are not credited here, and Katz through the education-technology race. The trio is therefore a defensible but not unique attribution.
assessment.maturity: The main papers date from 2013 to 2016, and a decade of replication, reassessment and extension has largely confirmed the central findings, with some debate about magnitudes and persistence.
uncertainties: Debate over the size and persistence of the China-shock effects.
The task-framework credit could pull in people not on this entry, and the 2024 prize already recognised technology and institutions.
Whether Katz should replace one of the proposed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data opened a new empirical programme on intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the causal impact of places and policies. The work is methodologically innovative and has strong policy relevance. It also reshaped how public and labour economists use tax and administrative data.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader. Hendren and Friedman are central co-authors on the mobility atlas, the neighbourhood-exposure studies and the Opportunity Insights projects. Katz contributed to Moving to Opportunity but is also credited elsewhere and is a less natural fit, so I leave him out.
assessment.maturity: The main results date from 2014 to 2022. Replication and extension are strong, though the ultimate verdict on long-run neighbourhood effects is still developing.
uncertainties: The work is relatively recent, and committees may want longer confirmation.
The mix of methodological and empirical contributions makes the intellectual core harder to isolate.
Attribution within a very large team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Melitz's heterogeneous-firm model of trade changed the micro-foundations of the field. It explained within-industry reallocation, exporter selection and a new channel for gains from trade, and it shaped a large body of quantitative and empirical work. It is a major step beyond Krugman's work, which was recognised in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (Econometrica 2003) is the core contribution. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to the proximity-concentration trade-off and FDI. Redding developed quantitative extensions, but those are later and more derivative. Helpman also appears under B013.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation. The model is the workhorse of modern trade, though evidence on the size of the gains from selection is mixed.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the Krugman prize and with the quantitative trade literature in B042.
Whether Redding or Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum, who sit in adjacent strands, should be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's alternating-offers bargaining model is a foundational contribution to game theory. It gave non-cooperative micro-foundations for bargaining and has been applied widely in labour, macro, political and market models. The Rubinstein-Wolinsky market-bargaining work adds decentralised-trade insights that link to search theory.
assessment.attribution: The 1982 alternating-offers result is clearly Rubinstein's. Wolinsky is the natural co-recipient for decentralised markets. Binmore made important contributions, including the Nash programme and work with Rubinstein and Wolinsky, but the central credit is narrower.
assessment.maturity: Over forty years of influence and long-standing consensus on importance, so it is a fully mature case.
uncertainties: Competition with several other game-theory and mechanism-design cases.
Whether the committee prefers a prize built on a single canonical result.
The relative credit of Binmore versus Wolinsky.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrate household heterogeneity and incomplete markets into New Keynesian analysis. They changed the understanding of monetary and fiscal transmission, showing the importance of marginal propensities to consume and indirect general-equilibrium effects. The result is a new standard framework for quantitative policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: The Kaplan-Moll-Violante trio (AER 2018) is a clear set of originators. The wider heterogeneous-agent macro tradition (Aiyagari, Huggett, Krusell-Smith, Bewley) predates and underpins it, and others such as Auclert and Kaplan-Violante's earlier work contribute. Credit is therefore partly shared with a broader field.
assessment.maturity: Recent, with the central paper dating from 2018, so the long-run verdict is still open. It is already widely adopted at central banks and in academic macro.
uncertainties: Maturity: the framework is less than a decade old.
The foundations in earlier heterogeneous-agent work, and a possible prior-recognition question for that tradition.
As a macroeconomist working near this area, I should discount for field familiarity, and I note that co-authorship ties with some heterogeneous-agent macro researchers could bias my view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, the New Keynesian synthesis and the theory of monetary policy rules form the conceptual basis of modern central banking. Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule and Woodford's integrated framework are central building blocks of that body of work, with large practical importance.
assessment.attribution: The credited list is very large and spreads credit across at least eight people. A three-person prize would have to leave out Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, whose work on estimated DSGE models and the inflation Phillips curve is significant. Calvo for staggered pricing, Taylor for rules and Woodford for the unifying framework is the cleanest division but remains contestable.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation, though the 2021-23 inflation episode has prompted renewed debate about the Phillips curve and the framework.
uncertainties: Contested attribution among many contributors.
Pre-existing recognition of the rational-expectations and macro-policy tradition.
Empirical performance of the framework after the recent inflation surge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh-Klenow and Restuccia-Rogerson showed that the allocation of resources across firms can account for a large share of cross-country TFP and income differences. This created a quantitative, measurement-disciplined research programme connecting micro data to growth and development, and it is a major advance in understanding income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (QJE 2009) and Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) are the origin points. Restuccia also made related contributions on agriculture and development. Rogerson, who is not credited here, is a co-originator, so the omission is a limitation of this entry.
assessment.maturity: The work is about fifteen years old and widely used, but debate continues about measurement error, the interpretation of wedges, and how much of the TFP gap is due to misallocation.
uncertainties: Disclosed connection: Klenow is a long-time co-author of mine (Aghion, Bergeaud, Klenow, Li, Boppart). I have not adjudicated this conflict, and the rank may be biased in either direction.
Omission of Richard Rogerson from the credited names.
Identification of wedges and measurement error remain debated.
